result.summary: Pausanias describes monuments in Messene: the Sacrificial Chamber, the gymnasium statues, and the tomb of Aristomenes with its bull-sacrifice omen. He then relates how Aristomenes was said to have aided the Thebans at Leuctra through the oracle of Trophonius and his shield.

scenes.title: Sacrificial Chamber and gymnasium statues
scenes.summary: Pausanias lists statues and tripods at Messene, including the wealthy Æthidas, honoured as a hero, and a possible namesake ancestor who was general when Demetrius attacked.

scenes.title: Tomb of Aristomenes
scenes.summary: The Messenians say Aristomenes' remains were fetched from Rhodes on Delphi's order, and they use a bull sacrifice as an omen. They claim he fought for Thebes at Leuctra.

scenes.title: Trophonius' oracle and the shield
scenes.summary: The Thebans tell that before Leuctra Trophonius ordered a trophy made of Aristomenes' shield. Epaminondas had it fetched and displayed, and it was later returned.
scenes.stakes: The Thebans face the Lacedæmonians in a decisive battle at Leuctra.

scenes.title: Statue and temple of Serapis
scenes.summary: Pausanias notes a bronze statue of Aristomenes in the race-course and the temple of Serapis and Isis.

notable_quotes.reason: The oracle of Trophonius tells the Thebans to use Aristomenes' shield as a trophy before Leuctra.

analysis.text: Pausanias blends monuments, ritual and local tradition, showing how Messenians kept Aristomenes' memory alive as a hero after liberation.
The Leuctra story reflects Theban-Messenian alliance after 371 BC and the founding of Messene under Epaminondas.

fun_facts.text: Pausanias cites Homer's unfired tripods, which he compares with ancient objects still shown in the Messene temple.

language_notes.text: Homer (Iliad 9 and 23) describes tripods 'untouched by fire', meaning new, never yet used for cooking; they were prized as gifts and prizes.
Palæstras were wrestling schools, often attached to or part of gymnasiums.
Honoured as a hero means receiving cult worship normally given to semi-divine figures, an extraordinary honour for a wealthy private man.
Demetrius, son of Philip V of Macedon, attacked Messene by night in 214 BC and was repulsed; he was killed in the attempt.
A cenotaph is an empty tomb built in memory of someone buried elsewhere.
At Leuctra in 371 BC the Thebans under Epaminondas defeated Sparta (the Lacedæmonians), ending Spartan dominance.
Plato, son of Aristo, argued for the soul's immortality in works such as the Phaedo.
Hexameter is the six-beat verse line of epic and oracular poetry.

context_notes.text: Epaminondas was the Theban general who defeated Sparta and helped found Messene in 369 BC, freeing the Messenians.
Aristomenes was the Messenian hero of the second war against Sparta; tradition says he died at Rhodes in exile.
Trophonius' oracle at Lebadea in Boeotia was consulted by descending into an underground chamber.
Serapis and Isis were Egyptian deities whose cults spread widely through the Greek world in Hellenistic times.

literary_notes.text: The dead hero's supposed fighting at Leuctra suggests posthumous vengeance; Pausanias's word 'amuse' signals mild skepticism toward the Messenian claim.
Calling his hatred 'eternal' turns Aristomenes' enmity into something that outlasts death, supporting the legend.
The god speaks in the first person through the oracle, giving the command authority and presenting the shield as a sacred object.
